title: Sharvari Showed Up in a Suit. Ananya Wore ₹2.3 Crore on Her Wrist. Welcome to Bollywood's Most Stylish Night.
excerpt: The BH Style Icons Awards 2026 crowned its winners at JW Marriott Mumbai — here's every look that mattered, every name that took a trophy home, and the one revelation from Boman Irani that had the room in tears.
body:
The fourth edition of the **Bollywood Hungama Style Icons Summit and Awards** swept into JW Marriott Juhu with the kind of energy that only a room full of people who dress for a living can generate. Daytime panels gave way to an evening of structured gowns, unstructured takes on masculinity, and one ₹2.3-crore wristwatch that practically needed its own security detail.

This wasn't just an awards show. It was a state-of-the-industry address — delivered in sequins.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=MSoYf5RoR4I</youtube>


## The Red Carpet: Five Looks That Won the Night

**Sharvari** stole the conversation before she even sat down. While every other star reached for a gown, she arrived in a tailored **Antonio Marras** suit — a structured tartan blazer with sharp shoulders and peak lapels, paired with wide-leg high-waist trousers, a crisp white shirt, and a grey checked tie. A ribbon belt added a pop of colour; geometric jewellery from **Maison Megh**, rings from **Part Time Saints**, and black **Christian Louboutin** pumps completed the ensemble. A sleek bun and soft coral makeup sealed the androgynous look. Nobody else in the room had the nerve to try it — and nobody needed to.

**Ananya Panday** went the opposite direction and leaned all the way into glamour. Her embellished black halter-neck body-hugging piece shimmered under the lights like she was engineered for red-carpet photography. The wet hairstyle — slicked back, editorial, deliberately undone — gave the whole thing a contemporary edge that kept it from feeling safe.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZ_8idICHDA/

**Pooja Hegde** chose a sleeveless maroon sequined gown with a clean boat neckline. The styling was deliberately understated — soft waves, a side part, minimal accessories — letting the fabric do the talking. It was old-school Bollywood glamour with the volume turned down just enough to feel modern.

**Manushi Chhillar** went full classic in a black bodycon gown with a sweetheart neckline and thigh-high slit, elevated by a statement necklace and matching rings. If there's a textbook for awards-night dressing, this was the annotated edition.

And then there was **Vaani Kapoor** in a strapless black **Georges Hobeika** gown, styled by Pranita Abhi — no accessories, chestnut waves worn loose, nothing but silhouette and fabric. When you look that good, less really is more.

But the wrist that launched a thousand headlines belonged to neither an actress nor a filmmaker. **Ananya Birla** — businesswoman, singer, producer — arrived in a pastel baby-pink bouclé duster coat over a white cropped tank and wide-leg denim (yes, jeans on a red carpet), anchored by pointed olive-green heels with gold detailing. The accessory that made everyone blink: a **₹2.3-crore watch** on her wrist. She left with the **Most Stylish Business Leader** award and a standing ovation for her film *Main Vaapas Aaunga*, which won **Iconic Film of the Year**.

## The Winners: *Main Vaapas Aaunga* Swept the Room

If one film defined the night, it was **Imtiaz Ali**'s sleeper hit. *Main Vaapas Aaunga* took home **Iconic Film of the Year** and **Iconic Filmmaker of the Year** for Ali, while **Sharvari** won **Mega Performer of the Year (Female, Popular Choice)** for her role in the partition drama.

The biggest individual honour — **The People's Superstar and Style Icon** — went to **Akshay Kumar**, whose *Welcome to the Jungle* is currently on a ₹100-crore run. **Shahid Kapoor**, riding the success of *Cocktail 2*, picked up **Icon of Indian Cinema**. **Ayushmann Khurrana** was named **Power-Packed Performer of the Year (Male)** for *Thamma*, and **Rajkummar Rao** took **Iconic Actor of the Year**.

On the women's side, **Huma Qureshi** — days before her *Baby Do Die Do* release — won **Mega Performer of the Year (Female)**. **Ananya Panday** added **Standout Performance of the Year** for *Kesari 2* to her evening. **Bhumi Pednekar** was honoured for her leading role in *Daldal*, while **Kay Kay Menon** received a **Special Mention for Acting Excellence** — the kind of recognition you don't campaign for but everyone knows you earned.

**Nawazuddin Siddiqui** won **Most Stylish Splendid Performer (Male)** and **Rakul Preet Singh** took the female equivalent. **Jim Sarbh**, who was magnetic in *Made In India: The Titan Story*, picked up **Mega Performer of the Year (Male)**. And **Arshad Warsi** — who's simultaneously promoting *Pritam and Pedro* and *Dhamaal 4* — earned **Outstanding Performance in a Leading Role (Male)**.

## The Anecdote That Stopped the Room

The daytime summit delivered its own moment of magic when **Boman Irani** opened up about the chaotic first day of shooting *Munna Bhai MBBS*. The late **Sunil Dutt** — returning to face a camera after sixteen years — was visibly nervous. Irani, watching him, convinced himself he'd done a terrible job and nearly quit. And director **Rajkumar Hirani**, overwhelmed by the weight of his debut, broke down and cried.

Twenty-three years later, *Munna Bhai* is a National Award winner, a cultural landmark, and a franchise with a third instalment quietly in development. Sometimes the messiest first days make the best films.

## What This Night Said About Bollywood Right Now

The winners list reads like a map of where the industry is heading. The biggest honours went to a mid-budget sleeper hit (*Main Vaapas Aaunga*), not the year's highest grosser. The red carpet was ruled by women who chose structure over spectacle. And the most memorable speech came from a man reminiscing about a film made before half the audience was born.

For the Indian diaspora watching from abroad, it's a reminder: the best of Bollywood has never looked sharper — or dressed better.
